articles.headline: FC 27 Title Update 1.2.0 Patch Notes
keyFacts: EA Sports announced that Title Update 1.2.0 will release for FC 27 on November 10 with gameplay adjustments.
The patch introduces changes to 95 Depth, fullback positioning, kick-off defense, and loose ball switching.
Career Mode will receive updates for UI, transfer requests, transfer status indicators, and Youth Academy menus.
body: Title Update 1.2.0 is coming to FC 27 on Nov. 10, and it will include massive changes. EA Sports has already announced the highlights we can expect in this major patch, and there will be plenty of tweaks to the gameplay.
Let’s find out what to expect from the next major gameplay patch.
Table of contents
Complete FC 27 Title Update 1.2.0 pitch notes 95 Depth
Positioning Improvements
Improvements in Kick-Off Defense
Improvements in Loose Ball Switching
Complete FC 27 Title Update 1.2.0 pitch notes
Gameplay is the main focus of this patch, and EA Sports has considered some major feedback from the community.
Title Update v1.2.0 introduces our first gameplay adjustments for #FC27 . Including changes to 95 Depth, fullback positioning, and more. Alongside key updates for Career Mode, FUT, and The Grounds.
Read the full Pitch Notes here: https://t.co/QcjkIj9OgJ pic.twitter.com/DlkP0t4Asp
— EA SPORTS FC Direct Communication (@EASFCDirect) November 9, 2026
95 Depth

95 Depth will be nerfed and position of defenders will be adjusted. Unlike previous instances, they will now drop off sooner while still maintaining the higher line. This allows attackers to have more space to build their attacks.
Positioning Improvements
Fullbacks used to drop deeper than intended when defending attacks. This has been adjusted, and fullbacks will now hold a firmer defensive line.
Similarly, attackers will do a better job at reading the opponent’s defensive line and make better runs to capitalize the space.
Improvements in Kick-Off Defense
The defensive line will hold slightly higher position right after kick-off, making it easier to defend against opponents.
Improvements in Loose Ball Switching
Auto-switching will be improved in loose ball scenarios, which also includes instances when a teammate performs slide tackle, headed pass, or when a shot misses the target.
Image via EA Sports Career Mode will also receive improvements in UI and other areas.
Addressed an issue causing players to incorrectly submit transfer requests despite regular playtime.
Corrected transfer status indicators and cleaned up action menus across the Transfer Hub and Squad Hub.
Fixed various loan and transfer flow errors, including out-of-season recalls and cutscene visual bugs.
Improved Youth Squad sorting and navigation within the Youth Academy menus.
Polished Central Hub simulation inputs, Social Media text, and general menu UI assets.
The patch will also feature plenty of minor fixes across multiple modes .
The post FC 27 Title Update 1.2.0 Patch Notes appeared first on Destructoid .

articles.headline: All carpenter locations in Gerudo Fortress in Zelda Ocarina of Time
keyFacts: Polygon reported that Link must rescue four captured carpenters at Gerudo Fortress in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
Players can sneak through the fortress or let guards capture them to reach the cells, according to the guide.
After releasing all four carpenters, a Gerudo guard will offer Link a mission to help find leader Nabooru.
body: The Gerudo guards captured four carpenters at Gerudo Fortress in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and it's Link's job to rescue them. By heading west of Hyrule Field, you will enter Gerudo Valley. If you cross the broken bridge — which you can do by riding Epona — you can talk to the Master Craftsman, who will ask Link to help his apprentices by sneaking into the fortress and releasing them.
Below, we show you where to find every carpenter in Gerudo Fortress in Ocarina of Time remake and the best route to avoid the guards.
Where to find every carpenter in Gerudo Fortress in Zelda Ocarina of Time

Releasing the four carpenters in Gerudo Fortress is the first part of the "Missing in the Desert" quest, which you start by talking to the Master Craftsman in Gerudo Valley. It's important to unlock the Hookshot before trying to complete this quest, as need it to get through the fortress.

To complete this mission, you need to sneak into the fortress, find the carpenters and open their cells while avoiding the guards. When you find a carpenter, you must talk to them to trigger a battle against a Gerudo guard. Defeat her to earn a key, which you must use to open the cell and free the prisoners.

If a guard sees you, there's no penalty other than being thrown into a cell, from which you can escape using Hookshot. While avoiding the guards is part of the challenge, letting them capture you is a valid strategy to quickly reach all four carpenters — and one that we will be using in this guide.

After releasing all four carpenters, the Gerudo guard will appear once again to make a deal with Link. By accepting the mission to help her find the Gerudo's leader, Nabooru, he will receive the Gerudo Pass, which allows you to move freely around Gerudo Fortress.

Below, we list the location of all four carpenters in the order that you can find them when starting from the jail on the north side of the map. You don't have to follow this order, but we believe this route avoids most of the guards.
Carpenter #1 location (Shiro)

You can find Shiro in a cell on the northern side of the Gerudo Fortress, entering the northernmost door, which is right after the stairs. The quickest way to reach it is to let a guard arrest Link, escape from the prison, and drop to the ground. Look to your left, and you will see a door. Enter it and, inside the building, you will find Shiro. Talk to him, then fight the Gerudo guard to obtain the key to open his cell.
Carpenter #2 location (Jiro)

To find Jiro, another one of the carpenters, escaping from prison is once again a good strategy. Jiro's cell is inside a building on the northern side of the fortress, an area that you can access without too much trouble by escaping from prison. However, instead of jumping down to ground level, stay on the ledge, and then leap to your east to reach the roof of the building where you found Shiro.

Enter the door in front of you to reach what appears to be a dining room with a long table and a patrolling guard. Wait for her to go to the opposite side of the room, then use the Hookshot on the candelabras. Once the guard begins to return to the other side, jump to the stairs below and follow the corridor to find Jiro's cell. Again, talk to the carpenter, then fight the guard to obtain a key and release the second carpenter.
Carpenter #3 location (Ichiro)

Ichiro's cell is in a room in the central area of Gerudo Fortress. Instead of trying to avoid plenty of guards patrolling the area, you can let them imprison you. Hookshot out of prison, and jump to the rooftop to the east. To your right, there's a ladder.
After climbing it, drop from the opposite side, and look to your left to find a door. Go through it to enter the building and go down the flight of stairs to find Ichiro.
Carpenter #4 location (Saburo)

To reach Saburo's cell on the southern side of the fortress, repeat the same route you did to find Ichiro. However, instead of entering the door to the left after you jump from the edge, you must go to the opposite side where you'll find a ladder.
Climb it and open the door in front of you to enter the room containing Saburo's cell.

Some of our favorites argue that Navi is unwilling to help someone who doesn't know how to drive, that Link is only here for the zipline-owl , and that this guy flipped his wife eight times . We also have a growing suspicion that there are no rules .

We highly suggest going back through the account's older posts, as they had a whole bunch from back when Tears of the Kingdom was fresh and new. Our own Darryn Bonthuys even took it upon himself to add one to the pile, but be warned: This is a very complicated ocarina song.

Crowds stretched for miles along Avenida del Libertador in Argentina's capital, with the faithful waving Vatican flags and chanting "Long live Pope Leo!" as the US-born pope passed in an open-top popemobile.
"It fills my heart with joy to celebrate... with you," Leo said in his sermon.

The pope also reinforced an appeal to President Javier Milei to protect vulnerable Argentines, visiting a disability care home struggling with the government's cuts to health care and social services.
What did Pope Leo say about Milei's spending cuts?
Before the mass, Leo visited the Cottolengo Don Orione care center in Claypole, south of Buenos Aires, which houses more than 400 people with disabilities.
He told residents their lives were a blessing rather than a burden, and challenged the idea that economic success alone measures a country's achievements.
"A nation's progress is also measured by how it welcomes all people with disabilities and particular needs," he said.

The remarks followed his appeal Sunday, at a reception attended by Milei, for economic growth to benefit people facing the greatest difficulties. He also urged leaders to choose their words carefully and recognize the limits of their power.

Milei became the president of Argentina some three years ago, Since then, his government has cut disability services and resisted implementing a law increasing funding for care, despite Congress overriding Milei's veto in 2025. The Senate is due to consider next year's disability funding in the coming days.
Argentina declares national holiday over Pope Leo's visit
Some worshippers camped overnight to secure a place near the Monumento a los Espanoles, where Pope John Paul II celebrated Argentina's last papal mass in 1987.
Monday was declared a national holiday to allow people to attend. President Milei and his sister Karina were among those present.
In his sermon, Leo spoke of families facing unstable employment, violence and addiction, while describing them as a pillar of society.
Where is the pope traveling next?
The visit is Argentina's first by a pope in nearly four decades. Leo's predecessor Francis, despite being born in Argentina, never returned to his homeland during his papacy.
Leo, 71, visited Uruguay before arriving in Argentina on Sunday. He is due to travel to Peru on Wednesday and return to Rome on November 17.
The first US-born pope spent decades in Peru as a missionary and bishop. The Vatican has described his South American tour as a "homecoming."
The demanding trip comes less than a month after surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his lung.

articles.headline: JD Vance Makes Lame Joke About 'The Devastating Loss Last Week'
keyFacts: Vice President JD Vance joked to reporters that a recent devastating loss referred to the Ohio State Buckeyes losing to Oregon.

body: JD Vance tried to make a joke about last week’s midterm elections. In the process, he proved to the world he probably shouldn’t pursue a stand-up career after leaving office.
During a meeting with reporters on Monday, the vice president said that “before I get into the meat of my remarks, I wanted to talk about the devastating loss last week.”
He continued, “There are a lot of people unfairly criticizing the leader of the team despite leading us to a great victory two years ago.”

He then referenced the loss had led to “a lot of staff infighting and questions about reshuffling,” and admitted there’s been “a conversation about whether the No. 2 has what it takes to ultimately lead.”
But the vice president wasn’t talking about the midterms at all.
“I’m talking, of course, about the Ohio State Buckeyes,” he said, which, like the Republican Party, had “a devastating loss” on Saturday, losing 41-28 to Oregon.
Vance, an alumnus of the school, tried to put a positive spin on the Buckeyes’ loss.
“Let me just assure you that I really believe in Luke Fahey, our backup QB, and I think our team will make an amazing turn.”

Vance’s “joke” got a few giggles from the reporters in attendance, but nothing close to a chortle, cackle or guffaw. His comment wasn’t the first time he had an awkward experience regarding his alma mater.
In April 2025, when the White House celebrated Ohio State’s national football championship, the vice president accidentally fumbled the trophy, making for an awkward situation.
Last week, Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.), who graduated from the University of Michigan, Ohio State’s top rival, mocked Vance in two ways in one sentence.
“JD… There is this delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in. Do you know what that means? Wolverine 1, Buckeyes 0,” El-Sayed said.

articles.headline: AMD confirms GPU driver bug is wearing out your SSD – how to stop it
keyFacts: An AMD utility bug is causing user storage drives to continuously write and rewrite data, degrading drive health over time.
Users and an AMD official reported the issue, noting that the bug persists despite recent patches.
AMD stated that a permanent fix will hopefully be included in the next update, while temporary workarounds are available.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- An AMD utility is causing drives to continuously write and rewrite data.
- A Reddit user reported that their drive’s health was being degraded.
- Workarounds are in place while AMD works on a permanent fix.

Under normal circumstances, an SSD might go all day without needing to access or write files. But for some AMD Radeon users, anything but normal circumstances are causing drives to continuously write and re-write data. The External Events Utility (EEU) that AMD installs alongside its CPU and GPU drivers is reportedly the culprit.
Also: Nvidia RTX 50 GPUs hit with more price hikes
SSD death by a thousand cuts

Reports of the issue first surfaced in July on AMD’s official PC user forum, with one user stating that the External Events Client Module and EEU were constantly writing information to their SSD after installing a Radeon 9060XT graphics card. Subsequent comments on the thread this month confirm that the issue has persisted despite several bug fixes and patch updates, with two users reporting hard numbers for data usage ranging from 0.3 MB/s to as much as 1.5 MB/s.
Also: The best laptops: Expert tested and reviewed

This week, Reddit user darklinkpower posted that the AMD Adrenaline Edition desktop application also had the EEU driver bug, using up to 1% of their drive health per month for around 16 months. That might not sound like much, but it can cause catastrophic problems if left unchecked.

AMD seems to be aware of the issue; a company official who goes by AMD_Vik on Reddit commented that it will “hopefully [be] fixed in the next [update].” While there’s little indication of how quickly a permanent, official patch will be pushed to users, there are a few ways you can protect yourself from the bug and prevent your storage drive from collapsing.
The workarounds
Solution 1: Disable EEU
- Press the Windows key + R, type in services.msc, and press Enter.
- Locate AMD External Events Utility.
- Open the properties menu, end the service/process, and change the startup behavior to Disabled.

This seems to be the most consistent fix for most AMD users reporting issues, but disabling the EEU can cause its own problems, such as disabling AMD FreeSync support or introducing display glitches if you hot-swap screens while your PC is powered on.
Solution 2: Disable ReBAR

The AMD Adrenalin Edition desktop app lets you control how your PC components communicate with one another, and it might be another facet of a complex problem. By allowing your CPU to access your graphics card’s memory, you can temporarily boost performance, but the EEU bug seems to let it and your GPU run rampant, eating up every bit of memory they can find. Changing a few settings within the app may help:
Also: I tried local AI on HP’s Omnibook Ultra
- Open the AMD Adrenalin Edition desktop app.
- Click the gear icon in the program, then go to Settings.
- Look for Smart Access Memory to be Enabled, Disabled, or Not Available.
- If it’s enabled, toggle it off to prevent your CPU and GPU from eating up your system’s storage and RAM.

This is a more niche solution that carries its own risk of introducing communication issues between your CPU and GPU, so I only recommend trying this route if disabling the EEU itself doesn’t resolve the issue. AMD’s official fix may be in the works, but without a firm timeline for release, users are left twisting in the wind trying to stop their PCs from hemorrhaging storage capacity.

articles.headline: AG Blanche clashes with CNN anchor asking whether it’s his ‘job’ to defend the Trump admin

body: AG Blanche clashes with CNN anchor asking whether it’s his ‘job’ to defend the Trump admin
By
Lindsay Kornick, Fox News
Published Nov. 9, 2026, 1:28 p.m. ET
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Attorney General Todd Blanche repeatedly clashed with CNN host Dana Bash Sunday after explaining how he and the Department of Justice will respond to recent Democratic threats to investigate the Trump administration.

Since the Democratic Party’s midterm election sweep, several prominent Democrats have used the opportunity to threaten legal action against President Donald Trump and members of his Cabinet. Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., who is poised to lead the House Oversight Committee, posted “lawyer up” in response to the midterm wins, as well as the news that Stephen Miller would be promoted to White House chief of staff.

Blanche defended Miller in an X post, writing that the Attorney General of the United States and the Department of Justice would defend the White House chief of staff, leading the “State of the Union” host to ask whether his job is focused on Trump Cabinet members.
“Do you see it as your job as attorney general to represent anyone in the administration being investigated by Congress?” Bash said.

“Wait, do I see it as my job?” Blanche responded. “The Constitution sees it as my job. Just in every administration, the Department of Justice represents members of the executive who are brought in front of Congress. So, there is nothing unique to me saying that. Every attorney general in history represents members of the administration.”

“And this idea that Congressman Garcia comes out and says, ‘Oh, no, no. Stephen Miller needs his own personal lawyer.’ I would suggest he read the Constitution,” he continued. “If he doesn’t have a copy, I can arrange to send him one. But the Constitution absolutely protects members of the executive, and I am the attorney general, and as that, like I do every day, we represent members of the administration who go in front of Congress. That’s nothing unique to me.”
During the interview, Bash argued that Congress has an oversight role and asked whether Blanche was concerned about that.

“No, no, no,” Blanche said. “They have a very unique role in oversight, I agree. Have you been listening to the rhetoric the past couple of days? You honestly think that all they’re doing is talking about their oversight obligations, when they’re talking about going after basically every member of the Cabinet? They’re talking about impeachments. They’re talking about going after companies, private companies, who happen to have made investments in this country over the past couple years. That is not oversight. I welcome oversight. Oversight is exactly something they should be doing.”

“So are you saying that you are going to investigate them?” Bash said, referencing Trump’s recent Truth Social post encouraging an investigation against Democrats. “And what you just described, is there a crime there?”

Blanche answered that depending on what’s said, there “could be” an investigation against some Democrats regarding their rhetoric against Trump. Blanche answered with a reference to recent remarks by Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., about hoping to discourage young conservatives from working in the government.

“You have free speech in this country. You are allowed to be critical of President Trump, of me, of this administration,” Blanche said. “But when the threats become so vile and so dangerous that you are telling people in college that they better be careful if they want to work in the Trump administration because somebody will come after them, at some point you have to draw the line.”

articles.headline: Trump says he sees no reason to escalate war with Iran
keyFacts: President Trump stated that he currently sees no reason to escalate the war with Iran, though Secretary of State Marco Rubio said talks are not close to a breakthrough because Iranian demands are unacceptable.

A British naval agency reported that a tanker was attacked and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, while Saudi Arabia's energy ministry reported a limited fire on its East-West Crude Oil Pipeline after a targeted attack.
French officials accused a cyber unit of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of carrying out nationwide hacks on commercial refrigeration in October, causing food spoilage and fires.
body: What to know about the Iran war today:

- In a that aired Sunday, President Trump said he does not currently see "any reason" to escalate the . However, he defended starting the conflict as "historically" a good decision, despite its economic impact.
- Mr. Trump is meeting Monday with the prime minister of , whose country has mediated indirect talks between the U.S. and Iran aimed at reaching a deal.
- Secretary of State Marco Rubio curbed expectations late Sunday, saying talks are not "at the verge of a breakthrough" because Iran's demands are "unacceptable"
Hegseth says he's not worried about impeachment
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said he's not worried about a vote on articles of impeachment that could happen in the House as early as this week.
"We're not worried about that," Hegseth told reporters Monday.
He said he planned to hold a news conference on the impeachment effort Tuesday morning.
Tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, British naval agency says
A tanker that was ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday was attacked, a British naval agency said Monday.

In a post on X, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center said that military authorities had reported the vessel was on fire, forcing the crew to evacuate, and that it had reclassified the incident as an attack.
The incident took place 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman.
UKMTO did not give any details on the potential perpetrator or the vessel.

Meanwhile, Iran's state broadcaster IRIB said Monday that four tankers had been halted in the Strait of Hormuz over the preceding 24 hours. In a post on X, IRIB said the ships were "brought to a standstill," without offering any further detail.
Both Iran and the U.S. have attacked ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz that they consider to be breaching their respective restrictions on the waterway.
Saudi Arabia's East-West Crude Oil Pipeline targeted again, energy ministry says

Saudi Arabia's crucial East-West Crude Oil Pipeline has been targeted again, the kingdom's energy ministry said Monday. In a post on X, the ministry said a "limited fire" broke out on a section of the pipeline in the Medina region, and that no deaths or injuries were reported.
There was also "no disruption to the pipeline's operations," the statement added.
An , which Saudi Arabia blamed on Iranian-backed militias in Iraq, put the pipeline out of action for several weeks.
Saudi authorities did not say who they suspected to have carried out Monday's attack on the pipeline.

Saudi Arabia is the top crude oil producer in the world besides the United States, and it has used the East-West pipeline as a vital workaround to export its products given insecurity for tankers in the Persian Gulf amid the U.S. war with Iran.
French officials accuse Iran of being behind store refrigerator and freezer hacks in October

French officials believe Iran was behind nationwide cyberattacks on commercial refrigeration in October, the Paris Prosecutor's office said Monday, accusing a cyber unit of Iran's powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of carrying out the costly hacks.

The Oct. 11 hacking attack , hitting "700 retail locations across France," according to the prosecutor's office, which said the attack caused "significant food spoilage and triggered roughly twenty fires" as the temperatures in refrigeration units shot up.
The attacks on the French grocery store chains were followed weeks later by affecting refrigerators and freezers at supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden.
In August, sparked an ongoing investigation by the Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division, Thomas Hamilton, a public affairs officer for the department, told CBS News.
Top UAE official says complete resolution of U.S.-Iran war and regional stability unlikely for "long period"
A senior official from the United Arab Emirates said Monday that the U.S.-Iran war was unlikely to be decisively settled for a "long period."

Dr. Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the president and a senior figure within the administration of the United Arab Emirates, said Iran was facing "one of the most serious challenges" in its history, with an ailing economy, pressure on its leadership and a "fundamental dispute" with the U.S. and international community over its nuclear capabilities.

"These factors make a comprehensive political settlement difficult," he said, referring to the ongoing war. "We should therefore prepare for a long period of uncertainty in which neither a decisive resolution nor a stable regional order can be taken for granted."
The UAE always opposed the war, he added in his remarks at the Abu Dhabi Strategic Debate event on Monday, according to a transcript provided by the Emirati foreign ministry.

"Our assessment was guided by a fundamental understanding of the region. Wars begin through deliberate decisions, but their consequences rarely remain within the calculations of those who initiate them," he said.

Gargash said it was "perhaps too early to fully assess the impact of the U.S. midterm elections on Washington's approach toward Iran," and added that the UAE would "reinforce efforts to pursue diplomatic solutions that can ensure lasting peace and stability in the Gulf."
Beach closed due to oil spill on UAE coast just south of Strait of Hormuz

Authorities in the city of Khor Fakkan closed a beach Monday after an oil spill was found along the coastline of the United Arab Emirates city, which is only about 20 miles south of the Strait of Hormuz.
Reuters cited a notice posted by municipal authorities on social media announcing the closure, without providing any further details.

Numerous oil tankers and other commercial vessels have been attacked and disabled during the war by both Iran and the United States, each claiming to act in enforcement of their respective restrictions on the key shipping lanes of the Strait.

Most of the ships that have been hit by missiles or sea mines in the southern waters of the strait, in or near shipping lanes close to the Omani and UAE coasts, have been struck by Iran. Tehran rejects the southern routes endorsed by the U.S., warning ships against using the lanes and demanding that they instead transit the strait via northern routes closer to its coast.
Syria denies report of troops joining Saudi coalition to fight Yemen's Houthi rebels

Syria's foreign minister said Monday that his country has no troops deployed in Yemen and is not planning to send any. His remarks came several days after Yemeni sources told the French news agency AFP that Syrian soldiers were in Yemen and Saudi Arabia to support the Saudi-backed coalition fighting Iran's Houthi rebel allies.
"There is no deployment of troops to Yemen nor is there a plan for such deployment in the near future," Asaad al-Shaibani said at a Monday news conference.

AFP quoted Yemeni officials on Friday as saying thousands of Syrian troops were set to deploy to both countries, and that some were already there. The report cited an agreement reportedly reached during a meeting last week between Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.
CBS/AFP
U.N. nuclear watchdog agency conducted inspection in Iran, foreign ministry says
The United Nations' international nuclear watchdog agency carried out an inspection of an Iranian nuclear site, the country's foreign ministry spokesperson said Monday.

Esmaeil Baqaei told Iranian journalists that the International Atomic Energy Agency conducted an inspection "a few days ago" in the city of Bushehr, which is home to the country's only civilian nuclear power plant.

President Trump has previously said he launched the war alongside Israel in February to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapon. Tehran, for its part, has repeatedly insisted it only uses nuclear materials for civilian purposes such as energy generation and medical work.
Iran suspended IAEA inspections at all of its facilities in the wake of on many sites by the U.S. and Israel.
Last week the U.S. military's Central Command announced a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear program.
Iran and U.S. continue to strike tankers in or near Strait of Hormuz

Iran's state broadcaster IRIB said Monday that four tankers had been "halted" in the Strait of Hormuz over the preceding 24 hours. In a post on X, IRIB said the ships were "brought to a standstill," without offering any further detail.
Both Iran and the U.S. have attacked ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz that they consider to be breaching their respective restrictions on the waterway.

Iran demands that all commercial vessels coordinate with its security forces to use shipping lanes in the north of the strait, close to its shores, and it has launched missiles at some it accuses of using southern routes that the U.S. insists are safe and open. Iranian authorities have claimed multiple times in recent weeks that ships using the southern routes have hit sea mines, causing fires.

The U.S. insists the southern routes are safe and open despite the ongoing attacks on ships using them, while American forces have attacked some commercial vessels accused of violating the U.S. military blockade of Iran's ports and vessels, intended to prevent the regime's sale of oil and gas.

On Saturday, U.S. Central Command said it disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, just east of the strait, after the crew "ignored repeated warnings and attempted to violate the naval blockade against Iran multiple times."
Oil prices continue cautious descent as Trump casts doubt on return to large-scale fighting with Iran

The price of Brent crude oil, the international standard, fell 2% early Monday morning to $96.38 per barrel, continuing a downward trend seen for more than a week as markets appeared to take hope from President Trump casting doubt on a return to full-scale war with Iran.
U.S. benchmark crude also fell, down 1.5% early Monday to $89.56 per barrel.

Oil prices have been up significantly since the U.S. and Israel launched the war with Iran, and Iran responded by attacking and threatening commercial ships in the key energy supply routes of the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. They remain about 50% higher than a year ago, before the war began, but down from highs seen during the peak of fighting, when Brent crude soared to near $120 a barrel.
Iran calls its proposed shortening of the implementation period for potential peace deal a goodwill gesture

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said Monday that Tehran's proposal to reduce the implementation period for a possible peace deal with the U.S. to two days from the previous seven was a "sign of goodwill."

Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told Iranian journalists that any deal with the U.S. must include the under the previous, so-called Islamabad agreement in June. That deal called for the lifting of U.S. sanctions on Iran as well as the U.S. naval blockade of Iran's ports, unfreezing Iranian assets and a ceasefire on all fronts in the Middle East.

"If the other side is genuinely even minimally serious, Iran can fulfill its own commitments within two days," he added. "We have already demonstrated that we are serious about fulfilling our commitments."
The previous ceasefire fell apart after several weeks, as Iran declared the continuation of the U.S. naval blockade a violation of its terms.
On Sunday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio downplayed the likelihood of an imminent deal with Iran, calling Tehran's demands "unacceptable."

The Trump administration has been pushing for Iran to agree to conditions on its nuclear program as part of an initial peace agreement, but Tehran has long insisted discussion on the topic can begin only after fighting and threats cease.
Rubio says U.S. and Iran not "at the verge of a breakthrough" on deal
Secretary of State Marco Rubio tempered expectations of an imminent deal between Iran and the U.S. late Sunday.
Before departing to Paris for a G7 meeting, Rubio said the two sides are not "at the verge of a breakthrough, while reiterating the president prefers a diplomatic solution.
"Right now, it hasn't been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable," Rubio told reporters.
He said he expects G7 allies to have a lot of questions about the conflict and next steps.
CBS/AFP
Trump expected to meet with Qatari mediator
President Trump is to meet with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House on Monday.
Qatar has been one of the key mediators in indirect talks between the U.S. and Iran aimed at reaching a deal to end the conflict.
According to sources cited by Axios, Al Thani, who is one of the key mediators in those talks, is looking to Mr. Trump to allow more time for diplomacy.
Trump says he sees no reason to escalate war on Iran
President Trump said in an interview aired on Sunday that he sees no reason to escalate the war on Iran and that he is "not looking" to do so.
"Well, I'm not looking to. I don't think there's any reason to," Mr. Trump told 60 Minutes when asked whether he was planning to intensify the war.
However, the president emphatically defended his decision to start the conflict in late February, while recognizing there have been negative impacts in the meantime.
"I think, historically, this will be a very good decision," Mr. Trump said. "Is it a good decision for today and tomorrow? Maybe not."
The president cited Iran's nuclear program as the main reason for starting the war, adding that he had done "what's right for our country."

Trump says new task force to extend naval blockade "is in full force and effect"
President Trump said Sunday that the new U.S. military task force to extend the Iran naval blockade "is in full force and effect."

Task Force Iron Gate is aimed at extending the success of the naval blockade to overland routes of trade, U.S. Central Command announced Saturday.

body: Just over two months after Vitamix launched Nano, its first personal blender, the company has released its first portable blender, the Ion. Announced on Monday, the cordless blender is designed for blending smoothies, shakes and frappés anywhere you crave a blended beverage.

Between the Nano and Ion, Vitamix’s 2026 focus seems to be on expanding its line with compact blenders. Laura Ostenkamp, Vitamix’s vice president of sales and marketing, said in a press release that the Ion was developed to give people more flexibility in how and where they blend, whether they’re at the gym, in the office or generally away from their own kitchen.

The Ion features a 24-ounce, BPA-free container with a handle and a flip-top. To blend your ingredients in that same container, all you have to do is double-click the Ion’s single button and the aluminum-enclosed, removable motor base and stainless steel blades will get to work.
More from CNET
With USB-C charging, you get 15 blends per charge. If you drink a smoothie a day, that’s over a week of drinks without needing to recharge.
Priced at $150, the Ion comes with a two-year limited warranty and is now available on Vitamix.com and at select retailers, including Amazon.

articles.headline: Trump attempts to cast doubt on Democrats’ midterm election victory, questioning early vote numbers and ballot machines – live
keyFacts: Donald Trump questioned the midterm election results on Truth Social after Democrats won control of Congress, reversing his earlier pledge to accept the outcome.
Outgoing Republican Congressman Thomas Massie is re-introducing articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over unauthorized war actions in Iran.
Lawmakers returned to Washington facing a December 11 government funding deadline to avert a shutdown before Democrats take control of Congress.
body: Trump casts doubt on Democrats' midterm election victory: 'Does anybody really believe this 'election' was honest'

After initially saying he would accept the results of the midterm elections, that saw Democrats flip dozens of seats and win control of Congress, Donald Trump has begun to cast doubt on the Republican drubbing.

“Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest,” he wrote on Truth Social. “How could the Polls be so wrong??? Some early voting ‘dumps’ were so large that it was impossible to win, no matter how many people went to vote.”
The president also repeated his baseless aspersions that that voting machines are unreliable. “It’s all about the machines, which are far more important than the voter!” Trump wrote.

Voting rights experts were initially concerned that the president and Republican allies would contest the midterm results, but after the seismic victory from Democrats last week Trump appeared to concede.

After last week’s elections, Trump said and his administration “look forward” to working with Democrats as they prepare to take control of both chambers of Congress. “We’ll probably work something out,” he told the New York Times.
In that same interview, he told the Times that he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results of the midterm elections.
Some Senate Republicans call to delay leadership election: 'We need to have serious discussions within our conference'
Several Republican senators have called on party leadership to delay the internal election scheduled for tomorrow (Tuesday).

“We need to have serious discussions within our conference as to what we can do to improve the outcome in 2028,” the group wrote in a letter to conference chair Senator Tom Cotton, noting the stunning GOP defeat in the midterm elections last week. “Holding leadership elections without engaging in a robust discussion and evaluation of how those running for leadership intend to lead would be political malpractice. It is certainly not the way leadership elections should be conducted in the world’s greatest deliberative body.”

Senator Ron Johnson, of Wisconsin, led the letter. However, there is no apparent challenger to the upper chamber’s majority leader, Senator John Thune. If Thune stays in place, he will lead the Republican minority in the next Congress.
Congressman Thomas Massie to force impeachment vote against Pete Hegseth
Thomas Massie, the outgoing Republican congressman, is re-introducing his eight articles of impeachment today against Pete Hegseth, in his bid to oust the defense secretary.
Massie, who lost his primary earlier this year, will likely move to force an impeachment vote against Hegseth again, ahead of Democrats re-taking control of Congress in the new year.
The articles include launching and continuing an unauthorized war in Iran, violating the War Powers Resolution without seeking congressional approval.
As we noted earlier, many House Democrats appear in lock-step behind the impeachment resolution, with some Republicans also expressing support.
Democrats have flipped the Georgia state House, the Associated Press reported on Monday.
As of Monday, Democrats had won 91 House seats and Republicans 86, per the AP.
The state House in Georgia has been Republican-controlled since 2005. The flip comes as Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won the governorship in Georgia last week.
Pete Hegseth has announced that he will hold a press conference tomorrow morning, marking the first Pentagon press conference since May.
Hegseth was asked by reporters on Monday whether he thinks he has enough Republican support to defeat the impeachment articles, Hegseth said, “We’re not worried about that.”
“Actually, I hope all of you will join us, we’re going to do a press conference tomorrow morning at the Pentagon on that very topic,” he continued. “So I’ll save my remarks there.”
Representative Don Bacon, a Republican of Nebraska, told reporters on Monday that he is “weighing” the articles of impeachment against Hegseth that were introduced by Representative Thomas Massie.

“We have eight articles, and I’m not very sympathetic to those articles, I feel like Iran’s waged war against us for 47 years, I don’t think the president’s done a good job at times, he never sought bipartisan support, which is a mistake, but I see a need to have gone into Iran” he told CNN. “But the areas that concern me most about the secretary aren’t in the articles of impeachment, the firing and redlining of 80 generals…admirals, the withholding appropriated money all year for Ukraine.”

He continued, “there’s a bunch of us talking about it, so this is, you know, Congressman Massie’s impeachment, he’s got more of a libertarian spirit to his write up, and I think some of us don’t feel comfortable with his justifications but I think there’s other ones out there, so I think that’s what we’re grappling with.”
Pete Hegseth, the Defense Secretary, today directed an overhaul of the Department of Defense’s Professional Military Education (PME) system.

A news release from the DoD states that “the directive reverses decades of academic drift, eliminating ideological distractions in favor of joint warfighting mastery, decision-forcing rigor, and competitive wargaming”.

“Under these new guidelines, the Department will evaluate military schools by a singular, uncompromising standard: ‘Does this program forge leaders who will win America’s wars?’” the announcement adds.

Some of the changes include establishing “warfighter chair” positions at all senior colleges, replacing “subjective seminar grading with rigorous, standardized end-of-course wargames and comprehensive exams to test tactical and strategic mastery” and eliminating “lifetime tenure and emeritus status for newly hired civilian faculty, shifting instead to three-year, performance-based contracts evaluated on teaching effectiveness and national security research.”
Democrat Chuck Schumer says Trump's 'return to election denialism was inevitable'

Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer has responded to Trump’s statement earlier today casting doubt on the midterm election results, saying that the president’s “return to election denialism was inevitable”.

Schumer added: “He can whine all he wants, but nothing will stop this inescapable truth: For the last two years of his presidency, Trump will face the largest Democratic congressional majorities in decades, all because he has been an unprecedented failure”
Commerce department stopped investigation into data company led by alleged Chinese spy after Nvidia intervention - report

A commerce department investigation into Megaspeed – the data company led by Singaporean executive suspected of being a Chinese spy – was halted after Nvidia’s general counsel intervened, according to a report by the New York Times.

This comes amid a probe Nvidia launched into Jensen Huang, the company’s CEO and founder, after he revealed that he had an marital relationship with the Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang (no relation).

According to the Times, Tim Teter, Nvidia’s general counsel, contacted the investigators at commerce department to inform them that their boss, Jeff Kessler – a top official – had given Teter permission to request details about their probe into Megaspeed. The case focused on whether the company was smuggling Nvidia’s artificial intelligence chips into China.

According to current and former government officials, and others familiar with the incident, that the Times spoke to, some viewed Kessler’s interaction with Nvidia as violating government procedure and potentially tainting the investigation.

The case was eventually transferred to the justice department late last year, but questions remain about Kessler’s discussions with Nvidia, and what information he subsequently relayed to Howard Lutnick, the commerce secretary or the wider Trump administration.
According to the Times’ sources, the justice department is conducting a criminal inquiry into Megaspeed.
Joe Biden will undertake only limited promotion of his upcoming White House memoir because of advancing cancer, the former president said in a social media post on Sunday night.

His new book, Promise Me America, which will be published on 17 November, is Biden’s account of a one-term presidency that began in 2021 in the shadow of the insurrection at the US Capitol on 6 January 2021 by supporters of Donald Trump eager to overturn the outgoing Republican president’s defeat by his Democratic rival in the 2020 election.

The deadly invasion of the Capitol as Congress was due to meet to certify Biden’s victory, after a rally near the White House where Trump urged his supporters to go to Congress and “fight” for him, remains a historic shame such that Biden in his book says of the current president that it “should follow him to his grave”.

In the post on X, Biden – who was diagnosed with an “aggressive” form of prostate cancer in May 2025, four months after leaving office – said the number of speaking engagements he can manage in support of his book’s publication will be limited.

“Some days are better than others,” he said. “It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down. What that means is, unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped.”

Instead, Biden said: “I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves”. He said he and his wife, Jill, were touched and grateful for the support of the American people since his condition became known.

The memoir takes an extensive look at the deadly violence in Washington DC fomented by supporters of Trump, who was seeking to remain in office after his defeat by Biden in the 2020 presidential election.

Meanwhile, the incoming class of freshmen senators who won their elections last week are on Capitol Hill for orientation meetings. This includes several Democrats who made history with their election victories.

Congress returns to Capitol Hill as funding deadline looms

House and Senate lawmakers are back in Washington after Democrats’ swept Republicans out of Congress in the midterm elections. This means that the remaining weeks in-session are likely to be ineffective as the GOP prepare to lost control. However, members do have one key deadline – 11 December.

articles.headline: How does Google Wallet's notification feed work and can you disable it?
keyFacts: Google released an update for Google Wallet in October 2026 that includes an in-application notification inbox.
The notification feed stores updates about saved cards, passes, travel information, and offers in one place.
Users can manage or disable these notifications through the Google Wallet app settings or device settings.
body: How does Google Wallet's notification feed work and can you disable it?
Here's how to check if you've received one of Google Wallet's latest feature rollouts.

If you've looked over the pros and cons of digital wallets and settled on Google's Wallet app, you'll be happy to know an update has dropped for the platform. This update, which began to roll out in October 2026, launched both increased passport recognition and an in-application notification inbox. This update has been added in an effort to have Google Wallet outdo Apple Wallet.
If you've received this new update, the notification feed is easy to find. However, if the thought of more notifications on your phone has you shivering, there are ways to keep this inbox quiet.
Where to find Google Wallet's new notification feed

If you have Google Wallet's new notification feed feature, there should be a bell icon next to your profile icon in the top-right of the app. If you click on this bell icon, you'll be brought to the notification feed. This page will be totally blank with a bell in the middle if you have no notifications. Otherwise, you'll find your notifications listed here. Remember, the feed is still being rolled out, so you might not be able to find this page at all.

Any notifications you receive about updates to your saved cards and passes will be stored here. This includes changes to traveling information (such as a gate change on a boarding pass), loyalty and gift cards (like point balance updates), incoming offers and more. This notification feed page will simply aggregate these notifications in one place, allowing you to keep track of them from within the app.
How to manage Google Wallet notifications

One of the reasons you might be happy to see this new notification feed could be rooted in a common problem with Google Wallet, that being the sheer quantity of notifications the app sends. The feed will allow you to find them all in one organized place.

However, depending on your settings, Google Wallet might be taking advantage of Nearby Notifications. Some cards saved to Google Wallet might be sending you offer updates depending on your closeness to a certain location. If you want to avoid notifications from your wallet, this notification feed isn't the thing you want to target. Rather, you want to disable notifications entirely or remove Google's ability to use location data to ping you. You only need to tap on your profile picture, head to Wallet settings > Manage Wallet Notifications and choose the settings you want to tweak. You can also head to Settings > Apps > Google Wallet and either choose Notifications to turn all notifications off or Permissions to deny Google Wallet from using your location.

articles.headline: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
keyFacts: Nvidia shares fell about 6% after chief executive Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with a woman alleged by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy.
Nvidia announced an independent investigation into the matter, though the firm stated it had no reason to believe national security or secrets were compromised.
China rejected the espionage allegations as groundless, while analysts suggested the financial hit to Nvidia would likely be short-lived.
body: - Published

Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 6% on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair.
Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China.
However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying "allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".

Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report, external.
The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.

Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation.
After the investigation was announced, other big tech bosses, including Elon Musk, came out in support of Huang to continue leading the firm.
US President Donald Trump said the Nvidia boss was an "honourable guy".
However, the news sparked a sell-off in Nvidia's shares, with about $250bn (Â£190bn) wiped of the company's market value.
While Nvidia shares fell, the US stock market opened on a positive note on Monday after last week's turmoil, with Nvidia's rival chipmakers benefiting.

But analysts suggested the hit to the company would be short-lived. Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist at Crossmark Global Investments said investors would not abandon Nvidia, because the chipmaker was so central to the AI industry.
"Nvidia is the core of this AI trade, and without them, all these other pieces start to fall apart because the financing's not there," she told the BBC.
Huang co-founded Nvidia, which is central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, with two other engineers in 1993.
Its chips were initially designed for gaming, but Huang decided to turn its focus on AI development, turning it into the world's second most valuable company.
Huang's position vulnerable unlike other tech bosses
A key concern for investors going forward is what would happen to Nvidia if Huang was removed from the company, as Fernandez said there was "no natural successor" to the chief executive.
Huang, unlike other founders in the tech industry, is vulnerable to any move by Nvidia's board of directors to oust him.
He owns only around 3.5% of the company, and Nvidia operates on a single class voting structure, meaning his stake would not be enough to act as a veto power over any board decision.
By contrast, many tech founders who lead their companies, including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta and Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, hold significant percentages of multiple types of stock in their companies.

Fernandez said she does not believe the board will remove Huang as chief executive, unless there is glaring evidence of wrongdoing related to national security or intellectual property, "but I bet they start bringing someone up as his number two, to have there for the future."
The modest fall in its shares mean investors believe it is unlikely he will step down or be removed as chief executive, but that the outcome of the investigation will be closely watched.

Even people who do not directly own shares in Nvidia can be affected by rises and falls in its value. Pensions or savings invested in pots which have stakes in the company through index tracking funds can be impacted, for example.
Nvidia chips have been a major focus of the AI race between the US and China and the White House has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold.
The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.
But Huang has been against restricting the sale of Nvidia's chips to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology.
In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.
Additional reporter by Samira Hussain, North America business correspondent.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy puts Nvidia’s China ambitions under scrutiny
keyFacts: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at an Nvidia customer whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect is a Chinese spy.
The Financial Times reported the relationship, and Nvidia independent directors are currently investigating the matter alongside inquiries from Congress.
The controversy threatens to complicate Huang's ongoing efforts to lobby the U.S. government for expanded AI chip sales to China.
body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has never been quiet about his belief that the U.S. should continue selling AI chips to China, rather than shutting the country off from the technology. The revelation that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy threatens to complicate that argument.

The Financial Times reported Friday on the relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer. Jensen Huang admitted to the affair and apologized in a memo to the company on Sunday. U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information about the CEO and influence the company’s efforts to loosen chip export restrictions.
Nvidia’s independent directors, working with outside legal counsel, are investigating the matter, and Congress is already demanding answers.

The controversy comes at a sensitive moment for Nvidia. Historically, China has been a big market for the company. It has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. In the three months ended July 26, Nvidia recorded $7.9 billion in revenue from customers headquartered in China, roughly 8% of total revenue.

Huang has repeatedly lobbied the U.S. government to expand access to China, and some of his persuasion tactics have been successful. Huang met repeatedly with President Donald Trump and administration officials last year; afterward, the government reversed restrictions on Nvidia’s H20 chips and allowed exports of its more powerful H200 processors.

On numerous occasions, Huang has publicly lamented export controls, calling them a “failure” at a conference last year and saying in May that it was “not wise” for the U.S. and China to create two distinct AI ecosystems. He has also warned that shutting Nvidia out of China’s compute market would enable the country to develop its own AI chips to challenge Nvidia internationally.

China is already moving in that direction. Reuters reported last week that about 600,000 H200 chips are being held in Hong Kong, awaiting shipment to mainland China. Beijing is pushing AI companies to prioritize buying chips from Chinese companies instead.

The idea that Huang needed any encouragement in the form of an attractive woman to push for greater access to China seems like a stretch, particularly because his lobbying efforts predate their reported meeting at an Nvidia event in early 2024. At the end of the day, Huang is a salesman trying to dominate one of the world’s biggest AI markets.

Still, the allegations involving Alice Huang open new scrutiny of the company’s business relationships and could taint any assurances Nvidia offers that it can prevent sensitive technology from reaching unauthorized customers.

Once made, rumors of questionable allegiances can be hard to shake. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly warned officials close to Trump earlier this year about Huang’s relationship with an alleged spy. Even if Nvidia’s investigation finds that Huang didn’t share secrets with his paramour, the question is whether he’ll be able to convince Washington that Nvidia can still responsibly do business with China.
Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment.

articles.headline: Workers feel pressure to use AI and show off to bosses — even when it slows them down
keyFacts: Half of workers use artificial intelligence to appease their bosses even when it slows them down, according to JobAssist data.
Nearly a third of workers hide negative feedback about artificial intelligence because leadership encourages its adoption, the report states.
JobAssist warns that these false adoption figures could skew artificial intelligence return on investment and lead companies to waste money.
body: - Half of workers use AI to appease their bosses even when it's not helping
- One in three say they've held back negative feedback about AI
- AI ROI figures are being skewed because of these false figures
Half (52%) of workers admit to having used AI despite believing they could complete the same task faster without it.

This comes as two in three (63%) workers say their employers now actively encourage or expect AI use for at least some tasks, with as many as 39% even highlighting their AI use to managers despite believing it didn't help their outcome.

The data from JobAssist ultimately points toward workers seeing AI use as a box-ticking exercise and something that's beneficial to their professional reputation and potentially career prospects – even though they don't see it as something that can always help.
Workers are boasting about their AI use to keep managers happy

Furthermore, nearly a third (31%) admitted to continuing using AI even after deciding it had not improved speed or quality, implying that workers might be worried that something could happen if they don't demonstrate a use of it.
A similar number (34%) also held their hands up to avoiding negative feedback around AI given that leadership encourages its adoption.

"If employees hesitate to report disappointing results, managers may receive an overly favorable account of how well their AI initiatives are working," the report summarizes, urging workers to be more open and honest about when they find AI to be most effective.

For businesses, false adoption figures could mean that AI ROI might be overstates. But with employers relying on these statistics to guide their AI strategies, it could mean that they end up wasting money investing in the wrong areas.

body: Nations Championship: England's Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry ruled out of rest of tournament
Steve Borthwick's side have been hit by a raft of injuries ahead of their Nations Championship clash against Japan; Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry have been ruled out of the autumn series
Monday 9 November 2026 18:38, UK
England will be without Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry for the remainder of their Nations Championship campaign after both players were ruled out due to injury.
It comes as Steve Borthwick's side has been hit with a series of injuries ahead of their clash against Japan on Saturday.
Seb Atkinson, who came off in the second-half of England's 45-22 win against Australia, is set to miss the match with a hip injury, along with Ollie Chessum (shoulder) and George Furbank (groin).
England are optimistic the trio will be available for their clash against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday, November 21.
Feyi-Waboso sustained an injury to his right ankle during the first-half of England's clash against the Wallabies, following a hip-drop tackle by Australia prop Angus Bell.
Bell was later sent to the sin bin, with Henry Pollock coming on to replace Feyi-Waboso on the wing at half-time. Pollock would go on to score twice.
The Exeter winger's absence could see Borthwick call on Saracens fliers Noah Caluori or Tobias Elliott for England's clash against Japan.
It would be Caluori's third cap for England, having made his senior debut during their Nations Championship clash against Fiji in July.
Centres Joe Marchant and Will Joseph could also be considered as wing options, while Fraser Dingwall or Max Ojomoh are likely to take the No 12 jersey in place of Atkinson.
Curry did not feature in England's win over Australia after he sustained a hip injury during training last week.
Borthwick revealed after Sunday's win that his brother, Ben Curry, was unlikely to start against Japan, despite the openside enjoying an excellent outing against the Wallabies.
It is likely Borthwick could deploy Freddie Steward at full-back in place of Furbank and keep Marcus Smith on the bench as utility cover.

England's 36-player squad returned to Pennyhill Park on Monday to prepare for this weekend's clash, with Jack Kenningham and Max Hicks both being drafted into the squad as back-row cover for Ben Curry and Chessum.
